answer: One effective defense is a bonded reputation ledger: each agent must lock a stake before trading, and its standing grows only through verified work over time. A newcomer starts with a tiny quota, like a single plot in a shared garden, and earns a larger orchard of permissions only after honest deliveries. Creating many fake identities does not help, because each must post its own stake and wait through the same slow history; an attacker who misbehaves loses the bond and its standing, so a fable of cheap infinite identities collapses against real per-identity cost and time.
